primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Regret definition:** reg(s_0,π) = V(s_0,π) - V(s_0,π*) (1) per MDP instantiation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_0': 'initial state, dimensionless', 'π': 'policy, dimensionless', 'V(s_0, π)': 'value function under policy π, utility units', 'π*': 'optimal policy, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: MDP with known state transition and reward functions; finite horizon; proper policies exist.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When policy π is suboptimal in all sampled MDPs, regret becomes unbounded.

primitives.name: Option-Based Dynamic Programming
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **DP algorithm:** exact minimax-regret optimization for independent uncertainties (but see corrigendum below); for coupled/dependent uncertainties, plan over *options* (n-step temporally extended actions) to capture dependence along option execution — trades computation for quality via option length n; stochastic option policies available.
primitives.assumptions: Coupled uncertainties require temporal extension of actions; stochasticity in option policies allowed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When dependencies between uncertainties cannot be modeled independently, option-based planning becomes necessary.

layer2.mapping: Encodes temporal dependencies in uncertain environments through extended actions (options), enabling minimax regret computation in complex domains.
layer2.telemetry: Solution time and normalized regret improvement over baseline methods.

primitives.name: Minimax Regret Objective
primitives.verbatim_quote: Can we instead optimize *minimax regret* — worst-case suboptimality vs the optimal policy per MDP instantiation — via a Bellman-style recursion, exactly for independent uncertainties and tractably (via options) for coupled ones?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'π': 'policy, dimensionless', 'ξ': 'MDP sample, dimensionless', 'reg_ξ(π)': 'regret under sample ξ, utility units'}
primitives.assumptions: Uncertainty quantified via finite set of MDP instantiations; policy evaluated against optimal in each sample.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when the number of samples grows exponentially beyond computational limits.

layer2.mapping: Defines a robust optimization criterion that avoids worst-case expected value conservatism by focusing on deviation from best possible outcome in each scenario.
layer2.telemetry: Comparison of normalized max regret values against CEMR and MILP baselines.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of minimax regret is to shift focus from worst-case expected value—which leads to extreme conservatism—toward worst-case deviation from optimal behavior in each plausible environment. This dual perspective enables robust planning without degenerating into inaction. The Bellman recursion defines how regret propagates through states and actions, allowing for exact computation in independent settings and approximation via options in dependent ones. In GSE’s context, this translates to selecting stake tiers that minimize the maximum regret across all plausible market worlds, ensuring resilience against model misspecification. The failure mode arises when the number of plausible worlds grows too large for exact computation, necessitating approximations such as option-based planning.
